Which school districts and village lines apply to a Cortlandt address?

The Tax Receiver collects for five school districts: Croton-Harmon, Hendrick Hudson, Lakeland, Putnam Valley and Yorktown. A Cortlandt address can therefore mean very different school taxes for houses a few miles apart. Name the district in any listing or offer packet, because buyers sort by it.

Village boundaries add another layer. The villages of Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson levy their own village taxes, and those are billed separately from the Town and County bill. If you sell a house inside a village, ask the village office for its bill and its collection dates as well. The Tax Receiver's office page links to both villages for that purpose.

When do Cortlandt tax bills fall due, and what are the penalties?

Westchester towns act as collection agents, so the Cortlandt Tax Receiver bills Town, County and school taxes. The Town and County bill goes out by April 1 and is due April 30. The school bill goes out by September 1 and can be paid in full by September 30 or in two halves, the first by September 30 and the second by January 31.

  • Town and County penalty: 2% in May, 5% in June and July, 7% in August and September, 10% from October to December and 12% from January to April.
  • School first half: 2% in October, 5% in November, 7% in December and January, 10% in February and March, 12% in April.
  • Penalties cannot be waived by any Town employee.
  • Prior-year taxes unpaid by June 30 become a lien on July 1, and a property with taxes unpaid after 21 months can be foreclosed.

The office bills over 15,000 parcels and collects more than $188 million a year. It is at 1 Heady Street in Cortlandt Manor, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. and on the last Saturday of April and September from 9 a.m. to noon. A drop box in the courtyard takes after-hours payments, no cash. Online payment adds a $1.00 fee for e-check or a 1.81% third-party fee for cards. Mail payments need a United States postmark on or before the due date, since postage meter marks do not count.

How do assessments, exemptions and grievances work in Cortlandt?

Cortlandt runs on a different calendar than most upstate towns. May 1 is tax status day, which is also the exemption and tax map change deadline. The tentative roll is published June 1, Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in June, and the final roll appears September 15. This year's Grievance Day was June 16, 2026. The 2027 date is Tuesday, June 15.

The Assessor's office says the prior year's final roll sets the current year's taxes, so the 2022 roll was used to print the 2023 to 2024 bills. A grievance is a challenge to the assessment, not the tax itself, and the Town suggests you ask whether you could actually sell for the full market value shown. Form RP-524 must be filed with the Assessment Office even if you plan to appear before the Board, and a mailed copy must arrive by 8 p.m. on Grievance Day.

Senior citizen and disability with limited income exemptions renew every year: the Assessor mails renewal forms in February and wants them back with supporting papers by May 1. If you are selling a house that carries one of these exemptions, tell the buyer that the benefit belongs to the owner and has to be applied for again after the sale.

Three recent changes are worth noting. Enhanced STAR no longer has an application, because the state verifies income yearly. The Town took over the Village of Croton's assessing function after the village gave it up in 2025. And a new exemption for veterans with a permanent and total disability rating needs local adoption: the Town scheduled a public hearing for November 17, 2026, the county and Croton had already adopted it, and the filing deadline would be May 1, 2027.

What do deeds and state transfer taxes look like for a Cortlandt sale?

Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division records deeds, mortgages and satisfactions, and it takes electronic filings. Cover pages, Form TP-584 transfer tax returns and RP-5217 reports must be created through the clerk's PREP portal. Deeds go back to 1680 in its online search.

State transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of consideration, ordinarily paid by the seller, with the return and payment due no later than 15 days after the deed is delivered. On a price of $1 million or more, a separate 1% additional tax applies to the buyer. For permits and any open violations, start with the Town and, for village addresses, the village hall.

More questions about Cortlandt, NY

Does a Cortlandt house need repairs before it can be sold for cash?

No. A cash buyer takes the property as-is and prices in the work. Expect the offer to be lower than a repaired listing, and check for open permits or violations first.

When is the next Grievance Day in Cortlandt?

Tuesday, June 15, 2027. Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in June, and 2026's date, June 16, has passed. Exemption applications are due May 1.

Who collects property taxes in Cortlandt?

The Cortlandt Tax Receiver collects Town, County and school taxes at 1 Heady Street. Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson bill their own village taxes separately.

What happens if I miss the April 30 Town and County tax date?

A 2% penalty applies in May, rising to 5% in June and July. The Town cannot waive it, so pay as soon as you can.

Where is a Cortlandt deed recorded?

At the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division in White Plains. File Form TP-584 with it, and build the cover page in the clerk's PREP portal.

Owners with a house in good order and no deadline can still do better on price by listing.

Haverstraw lies in Rockland County along the Hudson River, and the town includes the Village of Haverstraw along with hamlets such as Garnerville, Johnsontown, Ladentown, Mount Ivy and Samsondale. Sellers here deal with a town assessor, a town Receiver of Taxes whose penalty calendar is short, a town Building Department, and the Rockland County Clerk for the deed.

  • Agent listing: the usual path when the property is in good order.
  • Owner sale: keeps the fee, but you handle disclosure and contract work.
  • Cash sale: built for probate homes, houses needing work, or owners facing tax penalties.

How big and how costly is Haverstraw, per the Census?

QuickFacts gives Haverstraw 40,462 residents for July 2025, up from 39,087 in the 2020 count, a gain of about 1,400. Among homes, 64.8% are owner-occupied, and their median value for 2020 to 2024 is $387,500.

Rent runs a median $1,906. The town has 12,366 households of 3.11 people on average, the largest household size among the four towns in this batch, and median household income is $89,107 in 2024 dollars. Commuters spend a mean 30.1 minutes getting to work, and just over a third of adults (34.1%) finished a bachelor's degree. On 22.15 square miles of land, density was about 1,765 people per square mile when the 2020 census was taken.

How is the Town of Haverstraw laid out?

The town covers 27.41 square miles, but 5.26 of them are water, and it stretches across Rockland County's northern section from the Hudson River to the western county line. The village of Haverstraw holds the historic downtown, and part of Harriman State Park, including Lake Sebago, Lake Welch and Lake Kanawauke, lies in the west of the town.

Settlers took the name from the Dutch Haverstroo, oat straw, which described the riverside grasslands; a land purchase from local natives in 1666 was confirmed as a patent in 1671. The town was formed in 1788 and later gave up land for Clarkstown and Ramapo in 1791 and Stony Point in 1865. A calico printing plant built in 1828, a complex of some 30 buildings in Garnerville, now operates as the Garnerville Arts and Industrial Center.

  • Roads: the Palisades Interstate Parkway, US 9W, US 202 and NY 45.
  • Ferry: the Haverstraw to Ossining crossing of the Hudson, tied to Metro-North.
  • Bus: Short Line coaches run along US 9W toward Port Authority Bus Terminal.
  • Parks: Bowline Point Town Park and the Long Path trail.

About a fifth of the town's area is water, so a parcel near the river or a lake deserves a look at its drainage and flood history before you pick an asking price.

Which school district serves Haverstraw?

The Haverstraw-Stony Point Central School District is the one the Town of Haverstraw names in its tax collection notice, with parcels inside it eligible for installment payment of school tax. Under that arrangement, at least 50% is due by September 30, a second installment of at least half the balance by October 13, and the remainder before November 3.

Look at your bill for the district name and the installment option, since a buyer will ask what the school line shows.

How does Haverstraw assess property, and what are the dates?

The Town Assessor assigns a dollar value to every parcel, vacant or improved, residential or commercial, and that value feeds town, county and school tax. The office also handles exemption applications and the STAR program and helps defend grievances, small claims assessment review and certiorari cases.

For 2026 the grievance filing window ran from May 1 to May 28 and has closed, so the next chance comes with the 2027 tentative roll. The office provides a printable grievance application and a questionnaire for proposed assessments, so gather them before May.

What penalties apply to late Haverstraw tax payments?

Town and county tax is collected from January 1 through January 31 without penalty, and the Town of Haverstraw, a town of the first class, adds 1% in February and 2% in March. On April 1, unpaid tax is turned over to Rockland County Finance.

  • Installments: bills above $50 may be paid in four parts, with a 5% service charge and the first part due by January 31.
  • Later parts: April 15, July 15 and October 15, paid to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance in Pomona.
  • March payments: after March 15, checks must be bank or certified checks, in the office by close of business on March 31, with no postmarks accepted.
  • Cards: accepted, with a 2.45% convenience fee charged by the card provider.

Elderly or disabled owner-occupants of one-, two- or three-family homes can ask the Receiver of Taxes for third-party notification on form RP-923. A seller closing mid-year should ask the closing attorney which installment has been paid, so the proration comes out right.

What permits should a Haverstraw seller check?

The town Building Department issues building permits and Certificates of Occupancy and points owners to section 84-4 of the Town Code to see which repairs and construction need them. Those documents show that a house meets the codes for structural soundness and fire safety.

Before you list, confirm that every addition, finished basement and converted space has a permit and a Certificate of Occupancy on file. The department also handles questions about fire permits, burning permits, fire inspections and sprinkler systems.

How do the deed and transfer tax work for a Haverstraw sale?

Haverstraw deeds go to the Rockland County Clerk, whose land records page requires originals in recordable form, legible, signed and notarized. State transfer tax runs $2 per $500 of the price, rounded up, so the $387,500 Census median value would owe $1,550, usually from the seller.

The state tax return and payment are due by the 15th day after the deed is delivered, and the clerk takes them when the deed is recorded. A buyer owes a 1% mansion tax on a residence at $1 million or more. The clerk's land records page offers downloadable forms for the most common filings.

More questions about Haverstraw, NY

What happens to unpaid Haverstraw taxes after March?

Rockland County Finance takes over collection of unpaid bills on April 1. Until then the Receiver of Taxes adds 1% in February and 2% in March, and late-March checks must be certified or bank checks.

Is the 2026 grievance deadline still open in Haverstraw?

No. The 2026 filing window ran from May 1 through May 28. Grievance Day falls on the fourth Tuesday in May each year, so the next chance is spring 2027.

Can I pay Haverstraw taxes in installments if I am selling?

Yes, if the bill is over $50, with a 5% service charge and the first part due by January 31. Later parts fall on April 15, July 15 and October 15, so ask your attorney which have been paid before closing.

Which authority records a Haverstraw deed?

The Rockland County Clerk, which accepts only original, legible, signed and notarized documents. The transfer tax return goes in within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

Will a buyer ask for a Certificate of Occupancy in Haverstraw?

The town Building Department issues them to show a building meets code, and a buyer's attorney may ask for one covering an addition or conversion. Section 84-4 of the Town Code lists which work needs permits, and the department can answer questions.

The town grew 3.5 percent from the 2020 base to the 2025 estimate, a steady pace compared with towns that are losing residents. The renter share also means a house can attract buyers who plan to rent it out.

Which schools serve Guilderland homes?

Most of the town belongs to the Guilderland Central School District, which was formed in 1953 by merging eight smaller districts. It has one high school, Guilderland High School, one middle school, Farnsworth Middle School, and five elementary schools: Guilderland, Pine Bush, Lynnwood, Altamont and Westmere.

A few parts of the town are served by other districts, including Voorheesville Central, Schalmont Central and Mohonasen Central. Confirm the district on your tax bill, since the disclosure form has its own line for it.

What does Guilderland require for building permits?

Permits are required for most construction, renovation or structural work, and the Building / Zoning Department's FAQ gives the practical rules for sellers fixing a house before sale.

  • A complete application can take four to six weeks to approve, longer in summer.
  • All fences need a permit, and the fee depends on length. The department recommends a survey first, and it will not issue a permit over a utility easement without that agency's permission.
  • All sheds need a permit regardless of size or foundation, and sheds are allowed only in rear yards.
  • Permanent signs need a permit, but real estate for sale signs are on the list of temporary signs that do not.

The four to six week review window is the number to plan around. If a buyer's inspection turns up unpermitted work, a seller who starts the paperwork late may not finish before the contract's closing date.

How are Guilderland property tax bills paid and when do penalties start?

Town and county bills are collected without penalty in January, and school bills in September, according to the town's online tax search page. The Tax Office, in Town Hall on Western Turnpike, collects property and school taxes on about 12,500 parcels and also takes water bill payments for the Guilderland Water District.

The 2026 school tax calendar is already past its deadline. Bills were penalty-free from September 1 to September 30, 2026, a 2 percent penalty applied from October 1 to November 2, and as of November 3, 2026 unpaid school taxes are payable only to the Albany County Division of Finance. If the house you are selling still has an open balance, call the county before closing.

  • Payment options are in person, mail, a 24 hour drop box beside the Town Hall front doors, or online with a fee: $2.00 for an e-check, $4.00 for a debit card and 2.5 percent for a credit card.
  • Only a U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as proof of timely mailing.
  • The Receiver cannot waive statutory penalties, which are set by Real Property Tax Law section 924.
  • A returned check carries a $20 fee.

What can Guilderland owners do about assessments and exemptions?

The Assessor's office maintains assessments on more than 13,000 parcels and processes more than 1,000 deeds a year. It also receives copies of building permits from the Town and from the Village of Altamont, and it inspects the work to decide whether the assessment or the property inventory should change. A permitted finished basement or addition is therefore reviewed for assessment changes.

  • Informal review: submit the form and proof of value by April 1 each year.
  • Formal grievance: the town's assessment contest page lists May 25, 2027 as the last filing date for the next cycle, before 8 p.m., with an original signed RP-524 and two copies of supporting documents.
  • Exemptions: new and renewal applications are due March 1, except senior partial exemption renewals, which are due by grievance day.

Seniors, people with a physical disability and veterans may qualify for partial exemptions, per the school tax notice. If you hold one, tell your closing attorney.

How does a Guilderland deed reach the town records?

Your attorney files the deed with the Albany County Clerk, whose role the county describes as receiving, indexing, storing and retrieving documents on real property ownership. According to the town assessor's page, the county then uploads each deed and sends it to the town, and the assessor's office receives these uploads two to four times a month. A new owner's name can therefore take a few weeks to appear in town records.

Ask the Albany County Clerk for its current fee schedule, since recording charges change. Real property transfer tax follows state rules of $2 for each $500, as the Westchester County Clerk's deed guide explains, and your attorney can total the amount.

What should a Guilderland seller gather before listing or accepting a cash offer?

  • Your signed property condition disclosure statement under Real Property Law section 462, given to the buyer before any binding contract is signed.
  • Permit and certificate paperwork for any addition, deck, fence or shed.
  • The January town and county bill and the September school bill, plus the water bill from the Guilderland Water District.
  • Payoff statements, and any county tax balance.
  • A realistic closing date, given that inspections and permit reviews can each take weeks.

More questions about Guilderland, NY

Is Guilderland the same as the city of Albany?

No. Guilderland is a separate town in Albany County, west of the city. It has its own assessor, building department and tax office, and its own school district.

How long does a Guilderland building permit take?

The Building / Zoning Department says a complete application can take four to six weeks, and review can run longer in summer. Emergency repairs and demolitions may be handled sooner.

What happens to unpaid Guilderland school taxes after November 2, 2026?

As of November 3, 2026, unpaid taxes are payable only to the Albany County Division of Finance. Call the county for the amount due, including penalties, before the closing.

Do I need a permit for a for sale sign in Guilderland?

No. The town lists real estate for sale signs among the temporary signs that do not require a sign permit. Permanent signs and temporary banners do.

When are Guilderland assessment grievances due?

The town lists May 25, 2027 as the last date to file, before 8 p.m., using an original RP-524 form. Informal reviews with the Assessor are due by April 1.

How does a Clifton Park owner choose between listing and a cash sale?

A Clifton Park seller can hire an agent, handle the sale personally, or sign with a buyer who pays cash and accepts the property in its current state. The decision usually comes down to condition, timing and how much hassle you can absorb.

A listing puts your house beside every updated kitchen and fresh roof on the market, so a tired interior or an aging roof can leave a listing sitting. A cash buyer prices those flaws in and skips the open houses. You give up some of the top-end price in exchange for speed and certainty, so compare what each path leaves in your pocket after the mortgage payoff and the closing costs.

  • A listing fits a move-in-ready house and a seller with a flexible date.
  • A private sale fits an owner who has a buyer lined up and is comfortable with the contract and deed work.
  • A cash sale fits an estate house, a tired rental, a property with code issues or a job transfer that will not wait.

Where is Clifton Park, and what are buyers looking at?

Clifton Park is a suburban town in the southern part of Saratoga County, about 12 miles north of Albany, 7 miles northeast of Schenectady and 10 miles south of Saratoga Springs. The Mohawk River forms its southern boundary. The Adirondack Northway (I-87) and US Route 9 run through the eastern part, and NY Route 146 crosses the middle of town.

Growth came fast once the Northway opened in the early 1960s. The Census count went from 4,512 in 1960 to 14,867 in 1970 and 23,989 in 1980, and the town was the last one created in Saratoga County, in 1828. The area traces back to the 1707 Clifton Park Patent, and Eldert Vischer opened the Vischer Ferry crossing in 1783. The 2020 Census counted 38,029 residents and the July 2025 estimate is 37,775.

Which schools and neighborhoods shape a Clifton Park sale?

Most of the town, roughly its eastern two-thirds, belongs to the Shenendehowa Central School District, while corners of the northwest and southwest fall under Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake and Niskayuna. Buyers tend to ask for the district before they ask for the square footage.

Named places inside the town include the hamlets of Rexford, Vischer Ferry, Jonesville, Elnora, Grooms Corners and Clifton Park Center, plus the neighborhoods of Clifton Knolls-Mill Creek, Clifton Gardens and Country Knolls. The town advertises a 15-mile trail network, the Clifton Common sports complex and, on the river, the Vischer Ferry Nature and Historic Preserve with a stretch of the original Erie Canal towpath. Proximity to those amenities is worth mentioning to any buyer.

Does Clifton Park charge a Town property tax?

No. The Receiver of Taxes states that the Town of Clifton Park does not have a general town tax. The January bill therefore carries County and special district charges, and school tax comes separately from whichever district serves the parcel.

A buyer comparing Saratoga County towns may care about that. Still, the total bill depends on the school district and the assessment, so hand a buyer a real bill rather than a talking point. Special districts also appear: the Receiver's office collects for the Old Nott Farm and Rivercrest Sewer Districts. School taxes are never paid at Town Hall. Shenendehowa, Niskayuna and Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake each collect their own.

When do Clifton Park tax bills arrive, and what are the penalties?

Town and County bills are mailed December 31 and are due in January. The Receiver also advises that anyone who has not received a bill by January 7 should call.

  • January: pay the exact amount on the bill with no penalty.
  • February: 1% is added.
  • March: 2% is added, plus a $2 late fee.
  • After March 31: the Receiver stops taking payment, and the Saratoga County Treasurer collects instead.

The office takes payment in person at One Town Hall Plaza, by mail to a bank lockbox in Albany, or online by card or e-check, where fees apply. The Receiver's office says the bill prints from the Assessor's records and that all changes of owner or mailing address go through the Assessor. If you sell in the fall, send the buyer's attorney your latest paid receipt so the proration at closing is clean. Escrow lenders sometimes pay the bill directly, so confirm whether yours did.

What are the Clifton Park assessment dates and exemption deadlines?

The Assessor lists March 1 as the taxable status date and the last day to file exemption applications, May 1 for the tentative roll, July 1 for the final roll, September 1 for school bills and January 1 for Town and County bills. Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May.

This year's Grievance Day, May 26, 2026, has passed. The next falls on the fourth Tuesday in May 2027, which is May 25. The Town has been working to reach residents who may qualify for the senior citizen, disability and limited income, or veterans exemptions, and its 2026 notice set March 1, 2026 as the filing deadline. The assessor's office, on the second floor at 1 Town Hall Plaza, also collects data on improvements in the field and photographs them, so recent improvements may already be on record.

What local rules and offices matter when you sell in Clifton Park?

On the Town's own news page, a notice dated October 26, 2026 reports adoption of Local Law No. 14 of 2026, which amends sections 73-33 and 208-7 of the Town Code to define and regulate short-term rentals. If you planned to sell to a buyer who intends to run a short-term rental, read the adopted text at the Town Clerk's office first. Another notice from November 9 announces a hearing on a twelve-month moratorium on Tier 2 and Tier 3 solar energy applications. The same page tells residents that the last day to set out lawn and leaf bags for the Twin Bridges pickup is Sunday, November 22 by 5 p.m., which matters if you are clearing a yard before showings. It also carries a message from NYS DOT about the Adirondack Northway renewal project, worth a look for buyers who commute on I-87.

Deeds are filed with the Saratoga County Clerk at 40 McMaster Street in Ballston Spa, which accepts land recordings until 4:15 in the afternoon. The clerk's office reports digitizing more than 25 million documents. State transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of price, the seller ordinarily pays it, and Form TP-584 is filed with the clerk within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Ask the clerk for current recording fees.

More questions about Clifton Park, NY

Can I sell my Clifton Park house if it needs work?

Yes. A cash buyer takes houses that need updates or repairs, and the offer reflects the cost. Compare it with a listing price minus fixes, commission and carrying costs.

Who do I pay Clifton Park property taxes to?

Town and County taxes go to the Clifton Park Receiver of Taxes in January, with penalties of 1% in February and 2% plus a $2 fee in March. School taxes go to the school district, not Town Hall.

Has Clifton Park's Grievance Day already happened?

Yes. It was May 26, 2026. The next one is the fourth Tuesday in May 2027, and exemption applications are due March 1.

Does Clifton Park have its own Town tax?

No. The Receiver of Taxes states that the Town has no general town tax. County charges, special districts and school taxes still apply.

Which office files the deed after a Clifton Park closing?

The Saratoga County Clerk in Ballston Spa records it. File Form TP-584 with the deed, and ask the clerk for the latest fees.

What is the quickest way to sell a house in Carmel, NY?

Carmel sellers can hire an agent, handle the sale alone, or deal directly with a company like ours. A direct sale skips the wait for a buyer's mortgage approval, which counts for more at the price levels Carmel homes reach.

Carmel is the Putnam County town that borders Westchester County on the south, and it is also the county seat.

How expensive is housing in Carmel?

Carmel's population was estimated at 34,442 in mid-2025, a 2.5% rise over the 33,592 base from April 2020. Its housing costs run well above national figures.

Carmel measure (Census QuickFacts, 2020-2024)Figure
Share of homes occupied by owners85.4%
Median value of an owner's home$495,100
Monthly owner cost, mortgaged homes (median)$3,335

The $495,100 median home value compares with $332,700 nationally. The average commute of 41.2 minutes compares with 26.4 minutes nationally.

Who lives in Carmel and how long do they stay?

Households average 2.78 people, 19.3% of residents are under 18 and 19.8% are 65 or older, according to the Census Bureau. Roughly 93.0% of residents stayed in the same house over the past year, and 43.4% of adults hold a four-year degree or more.

About 13.0% of residents were born abroad, 17.5% are Hispanic or Latino, and one in five residents aged 5 or older speaks a language other than English at home. Broadband reaches 95.2% of households, and 4.4% of residents are below the poverty line. A typical mortgaged owner pays $3,335 a month, so a missed payment or two adds up quickly. If you are behind or owe close to what the house is worth, request a payoff letter from your lender before comparing offers.

Where is the town of Carmel and what is inside it?

Carmel sits on the southern edge of Putnam County, about 50 miles north of New York City and 10 miles west of Danbury, Connecticut. The town covers 40.69 square miles, with 35.91 of land and 4.79 of water, so water covers about 11% of the town.

The southern town line is the Westchester County border, next to Somers and Yorktown. There are no incorporated villages. Instead the town has hamlets, and the two largest, Carmel and Mahopac, are big enough to pass for villages. Others include Baldwin Place and Carmel Hills. Town Hall is at 60 McAlpin Avenue in Mahopac, even though the county seat sits in the Carmel hamlet in the northeastern corner of the town, and ZIP codes 10512 and 10541 both apply. Use the address on your deed and tax bill when you start paperwork.

How did Carmel come to be the Putnam County seat?

Wappinger people lived on this land until a 1691 sale to Dutch traders, and a settler named Hughson arrived around 1740. Carmel was formed in 1795 while still part of Dutchess County. When Putnam County was created in 1812, Carmel became the county seat.

The original Putnam County Court House, built in 1814, is among the oldest working courthouses in New York State, and a newer courthouse opened on Gleneida Avenue in early 2008. If your house relies on a well or septic system, the county's Public Access Portal already holds records for those systems, so check it before a buyer asks.

Which schools and services serve Carmel homes?

Two districts cover most of the town, and the parcel decides which one a buyer's children attend.

  • Carmel Central School District, whose Carmel High School on Fair Street serves 1,843 students according to Wikipedia
  • Mahopac Central School District, which runs six public schools for 4,132 students
  • Smaller slices of the town fall in Lakeland, North Salem and Brewster districts

The Town of Carmel Police Department handles law enforcement, supported by the Putnam County Sheriff's Office and the State Police. Fire protection comes from the Carmel Fire Department, Croton Falls Fire District, Mahopac Volunteer Fire Department and Mahopac Falls Volunteer Fire Department. Putnam Hospital Center, a 164-bed hospital on Stoneleigh Avenue, opened in 1964.

Tornadoes have touched down near the center of town, including an F-2 on July 10, 1989 that crossed Fair Street and caused between $5 million and $50 million in damage.

What should I ask the Town of Carmel before I list?

Ask the Town of Carmel Building Department, at Town Hall, 60 McAlpin Avenue, whether any permit on the house was left open and whether a certificate of occupancy exists for additions, decks, finished basements and garages. Unclosed permits tend to surface when a buyer's attorney orders a title and municipal search, and a cash buyer can take the house with those items still open. Ask the assessor for the current assessed value and any exemptions on the parcel.

How does the Putnam County Clerk handle a Carmel sale?

The Putnam County Clerk's Office at 40 Gleneida Avenue in Carmel sees customers by appointment only; the number is 845-808-1142. Office hours are 9am to 5pm Monday through Friday, with summer hours of 8am to 4pm from mid-June through mid-September. Land recordings can go in the dropbox outside the County Office Building, and the clerk asks filers to consider e-recording through one of its partners. The office offers a Land Records Search and a fillable RP-5217 transfer report form.

The clerk also offers a free Fraud Alert service that emails you whenever a document is filed under your name. Owners of a vacant house, such as an inherited one, can sign up through the clerk's page.

New York's state transfer tax is $2.00 per $500 of price. Ask the Putnam County Clerk for the exact amount that applies to your TP-584 filing before you sign.

How do Carmel property assessments and tax relief work?

The Carmel Assessor's Office is at 60 McAlpin Avenue in Mahopac, phone 845-628-1500. The county's Real Property Tax Service Agency at 40 Gleneida Avenue, phone 845-808-1030, runs the Beacon property search and publishes tax rolls and rates.

The county's real property agency lists these exemptions under the Real Property Tax Law:

  • Senior citizens aged 65 and over (section 467)
  • Persons with disabilities (section 459-c)
  • Alternative veterans (section 458-a) and Cold War veterans (section 458-b)
  • Volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers (section 466-a)
  • Forest land (section 480-a) and agricultural land (section 305)

An owner who thinks an assessment is too high starts with the local Board of Assessment Review. After a denial, a resident owner of residential property can petition for Small Claims Assessment Review, and the clerk's page gives a deadline of 30 days after the final roll is filed. SCAR petitions must be filed electronically.

More questions about Carmel, NY

Is Carmel a town or a village?

Carmel is a town, and it has no incorporated villages. Carmel and Mahopac are hamlets inside it, and Town Hall sits at 60 McAlpin Avenue in Mahopac.

Where is a Carmel deed recorded?

The Putnam County Clerk's Office, 40 Gleneida Avenue in Carmel, takes recordings. Visits are by appointment, and land documents can be left in the dropbox or e-recorded through a partner.

Which office handles my Carmel assessment?

The Carmel Assessor's Office, at 60 McAlpin Avenue in Mahopac, phone 845-628-1500. The county's Real Property Tax Service Agency, 845-808-1030, helps with tax rolls and exemption questions.

Can I contest my Carmel assessment before selling?

If you live in the house, yes. Begin with the local Board of Assessment Review. After a denial you may file a Small Claims Assessment Review petition, electronically, within 30 days after the final roll.

Which school district covers my Carmel house?

Most of the town falls in Carmel Central or Mahopac Central, and smaller areas in Lakeland, North Salem and Brewster. Because the line follows the parcel, verify it with the district before quoting it to a buyer.

Ithaca at a glance

  • Ithaca is in Tompkins County.
Selling in Ithaca?
We buy Ithaca houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Taxes on the sale itself

See the transfer tax guide.

What should I know before selling a house in Ithaca, NY?

Ithaca is a university city where renters outnumber owners, so the first question for most sellers is whether the house has ever been a rental. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 29.6% for 2020-2024, with 14,167 households and an average of 1.71 people each, and that mix shapes both the buyer pool and the city paperwork.

The city sits at the south end of Cayuga Lake in Tompkins County, and the surrounding Town of Ithaca is a legally separate municipality, so confirm which one covers your address. Estimated population on July 1, 2025 was 33,632, a gain of 4.8% from the 2020 base of 32,085. Only 54.2% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which shows how often households here turn over. A seller should decide early whether the likely buyer is an owner-occupant, an investor who wants rental income, or a cash buyer who will take the house as it stands.

  • Owner-occupied houses on East Hill, West Hill and South Hill usually sell to buyers who plan to live in them.
  • Houses near Collegetown or with accessory apartments draw investors, who will ask about the rental certificate.
  • Houses that need work or carry tenants may sell fastest to a buyer who pays cash.

How is Ithaca laid out, and why does it matter to a seller?

Ithaca was built on flat land at the south end of Cayuga Lake and then spread up three hillsides: East Hill, West Hill and South Hill. Cornell University sits on East Hill, between the Fall Creek and Cascadilla Creek gorges, and Ithaca College moved to South Hill in the 1960s.

That terrain gives the city steep streets, creek gorges and older frame houses on small lots. A seller on a hillside lot should expect questions about drainage, retaining walls and winter access. Buyers coming from outside the area often ask about driving, and Wikipedia notes that every trip into Ithaca involves two-lane state highways, with the city sitting at the junction of Routes 13, 13A, 34, 79, 89, 96, 96B and 366. New York City is about 225 miles away, and Binghamton and Syracuse are each roughly an hour by car.

Education drives the local economy. Cornell opened in 1865 and Ithaca College began in 1892 as a conservatory, and the Ithaca City School District, which Wikipedia describes as serving about 5,500 students, covers the city and the area around it. Collegetown, next to the Cornell campus, has seen many new apartment buildings, and the Ithaca Commons pedestrian mall anchors the downtown.

What do the Census numbers show for Ithaca home values and rents?

The median value of an owner-occupied home in the city is $342,700 for 2020-2024, and median gross rent is $1,447. Median monthly owner costs are $2,368 with a mortgage and $994 without one.

Household income is $48,784 at the median, and per-capita income is $31,599, while 67.7% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The poverty rate is 30.4%, a figure shaped by the large student population. Because the city's land area is only 5.39 square miles and the 2020 density was 5,958 people per square mile, the housing stock is tight, and even a modest house can draw several showings in a good season.

Mean travel time to work is 18.7 minutes. That short commute, plus the Cornell and Ithaca College job base, is why buyers pay attention to walkable addresses. Retail and food-service sales per Census data give a sense of the city's visitor economy: accommodation and food services totaled about $200 million in 2022.

What does the City of Ithaca require for rental housing and short-term rentals?

The City requires a housing inspection and a Certificate of Compliance for residential rental dwellings, and a buyer who plans to rent the property will check that the certificate is current. The rule covers one- and two-family dwellings, multiple dwellings, dormitories, fraternities, sororities, mixed-use buildings with residential units and accessory apartments in single-family homes.

Fees depend on the building type. The Building Division bills the property owner once the inspection is done, and payment is due within 30 days. Owners get one 30-day extension per property to prepare for an inspection or to fix violations without added violation charges.

Certificate of Compliance itemFeeSource
One-family dwelling, initial inspection$100City of Ithaca fee schedule
Two-family dwelling, initial inspection$175City of Ithaca fee schedule
Apartment house with 3 to 8 units$300City of Ithaca fee schedule
Each violation found at the initial inspection$10City of Ithaca fee schedule
Each violation still uncorrected at re-inspection$50City of Ithaca fee schedule
Re-inspection trip$75 per hour, $75 minimumCity of Ithaca fee schedule

Short-term rentals add a permit on top of the Certificate of Compliance. The city's host guide says the permit lasts one year, the permit number must appear in every listing, a local contact must respond within 60 minutes, and hosts collect both a Tompkins County and a City of Ithaca hotel room occupancy tax, each at 5%. If a buyer is purchasing your house as a short-term rental, ask the Building Division at 108 E. Green Street whether the permit transfers or must be reissued. The division's phone line for housing inspections is (607) 274-6509.

How is a deed recorded in Tompkins County, and what does it cost?

The Tompkins County Clerk is the registrar of deeds for Ithaca, and the clerk's published schedule lists the first page of a deed at $50 with each added page at $5. A $10 deed notice applies to residential deeds recorded since March 11, 2020, and the TP-584 transfer tax return costs $5.

The clerk lists the transfer tax as $6 per $1,000. The RP-5217 real property transfer report carries a $125 fee when the property is residential and $250 otherwise. Sellers who live out of state must file form IT-2663, which the state revises every year, so a printed copy from an earlier year will not do. Payment at the clerk's counter is by cash or check.

Searching land records costs $5 per name for records back to 1968 when clerk staff perform the search, and copies are $0.65 a page with a $1.30 minimum. For a seller, the practical point is that the closing attorney or title company handles these filings, but it helps to know that Tompkins County's numbers differ from Suffolk or Chautauqua County, so a settlement statement copied from a past sale elsewhere in New York will not match.

How do winters and gorges affect an Ithaca house sale?

Ithaca averages about 67 inches of snow a year, and frost can arrive at any time except midsummer. The average first freeze is October 5 and the last is May 15, which gives the area a 141-day growing season and a USDA hardiness zone between 5b and 6a.

Inspectors look closely at roofs, gutters, foundations and heating systems in a climate like this. A buyer will ask the age of the furnace, whether pipes in exterior walls have frozen, and how water drains off the lot after spring melt. Summers are warm and brief, with afternoon thunderstorms and the occasional heat wave that reaches the mid-90s to 100 degrees, so a house with no cooling is still sellable but may prompt a lower offer.

  • Gather heating, roof and foundation records before the first showing.
  • Photograph the house in a dry season if the basement ever took on water.
  • Clear gutters and walkways before an inspection in the colder months.

Is a cash offer a good fit for an Ithaca house?

A cash offer fits when the house has rental violations, deferred repairs or tenants in place, since those problems slow a financed sale. For a clean owner-occupied house in a desirable neighborhood, an open-market listing may bring more.

Get any offer in writing, ask how the buyer handles an expired Certificate of Compliance or open violations, and confirm that a New York real estate attorney will review the contract. Compare the price with what you would net after commission, repairs and carrying costs over several months. Selling a student rental also raises timing questions, so ask the buyer in advance how existing leases would be handled.

More questions about Ithaca, NY

Does Ithaca require a certificate before I sell a rental house?

The city requires a Certificate of Compliance for residential rental dwellings, issued after a housing inspection by the Building Division. A buyer who intends to keep renting will usually want it current, so schedule the inspection early. The division accepts inspection applications online.

How much is a Certificate of Compliance for a one-family house in Ithaca?

The initial inspection fee is $100 for a one-family dwelling and $175 for a two-family dwelling. Each violation found adds $10, and each violation still uncorrected at re-inspection costs $50. A return trip is billed at $75 per hour with a $75 minimum.

What does it cost to record a deed in Tompkins County?

The Tompkins County Clerk charges $50 for the first page of a deed and $5 for each added page. Add a $10 deed notice, a $5 TP-584 filing and the RP-5217 fee of $125 for residential property. The clerk lists the transfer tax at $6 per $1,000.

How many people live in the City of Ithaca?

The Census Bureau estimates 33,632 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is up 4.8% from the 2020 base. The city covers 5.39 square miles of land.

Can I sell my Ithaca house if it has an Airbnb permit?

Yes. Ask the Building Division whether a new owner has to apply for a fresh permit. The permit lasts one year, it depends on a current Certificate of Compliance, and hosts collect separate 5% city and county occupancy taxes.

Where is Clarence, NY, and how did the town grow?

Clarence sits in the northeastern part of Erie County, northeast of Buffalo, and it was the first town established in the county, in 1808. Tonawanda Creek forms the northern boundary with Niagara County. One of the first settlers, Asa Ransom, arrived in 1799 in the area now called Clarence Hollow, and the town takes its name from Prince William, Duke of Clarence.

Brick kilns, potash and gypsum mining brought industry by the end of the nineteenth century, and quarries followed. Today the town is partly suburban and partly light industry and farmland. It has no incorporated villages, and the town government offices are in the Clarence Center area.

  • The town covers 53.63 square miles, nearly all of it land.
  • The 2020 census counted 32,950 residents, a 7.4 percent increase over 2010.
  • Nearby towns include Amherst to the west, Lancaster to the south, Newstead to the east, and Lockport and Royalton in Niagara County to the north.

Which Clarence hamlets and schools matter to a buyer?

Clarence is a collection of hamlets rather than one downtown. Clarence Hollow is the main district in the southeast, Clarence Center sits near the middle of town around Goodrich Road and Clarence Center Road, and Harris Hill occupies the southwest corner. Swormville, Millersport and East Amherst lie along the western and northern borders and extend into neighboring towns. Spaulding Lake is an upscale housing project built around a former quarry north of Main Street, and Rock Oak Estates is a 55-plus community on Main Street.

Most of the town is in the Clarence Central School District, with one high school, one middle school and four elementary schools: Clarence Center, Harris Hill, Ledgeview and Sheridan Hill. A portion of the town belongs to the Williamsville Central School District. Two Catholic parish schools serve kindergarten through eighth grade, one in Harris Hill and one in Swormville.

  • The ZIP codes in town are 14031, 14032, 14051 and 14221.
  • New York Route 5 (Main Street) crosses the southern half of the town.
  • Transit Road (Route 78) marks the west line, and Sheridan Drive (Route 324) ends at Main Street.
  • The Thruway runs just south of town and clips a small southeastern corner.

How do I challenge a Clarence assessment?

The town says a property should be assessed at 100 percent of full market value, and it gives owners a three-step path to contest the number. The informal review accepts applications from January 1 to March 28. You are asked to show reasonable evidence based on market sales, and the town warns against comparing unlike houses, such as a five-year-old house to a fifty-year-old one or a house in a different neighborhood.

The formal step is the Board of Assessment Review on Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday in May, which will be May 25 in 2027. Form RP-524 is used only for that board and should not be used for the informal review. Owners who still disagree can ask for a small claims assessment review, and the town posts SCAR instructions and an assessment timetable on its assessment cycle page.

The town also runs an online Property Record Online System for looking up parcel data and the informal review worksheets, which become available after January 1. Check the record there for errors before you list.

What are the Clarence tax due dates and penalties?

The Town Clerk's office collects property tax in Clarence, from the Town Hall at One Town Place. Town and county bills go out by mid-January and are due on or about February 15. School bills go out by mid-September and are due on or about October 15. If your taxes are in escrow, you receive a receipt after the bank pays rather than a bill.

Town and county payment windowPenalty
February 16 to 281.5%
March 1 to 153.0%
March 16 to 314.5%
April 1 to 156.0%
April 16 to 307.5%

On May 1 a 7.5 percent penalty joins the levy, and 1.5 percent interest accrues monthly until unpaid taxes are sold in November, at which point the total reaches 18.78 percent. After June 30, unpaid town and county taxes move to Erie County Finance. School taxes carry a 7.5 percent penalty from October 16 to 31 and 9 percent in November, and unpaid school balances are re-levied onto the next town and county bill. Partial payments of any amount are accepted. If you sold a parcel, forward the bill to the new owner or call the Clerk so the office can locate them.

What should I know about Clarence permits before I list?

Clarence requires permits for new construction, additions, conversions, pools, decks, sheds, walls, reroofing, and for plumbing, heating, cooling and electrical changes, including generators. Fence and sign permits come from Planning and Zoning, and driveway permits come from the County, State or Town Highway Department. The Building Department is at 6221 Goodrich Road, and the Town Clerk collects permit fees.

The town's own FAQ speaks directly to resale. Work done without a required permit may hold up the sale of your property and may affect an insurance claim, and the town can issue a stop work order. Every permitted project needs inspections and a certificate of occupancy or compliance before the space is used, and the department says its officers average about 15 inspections on a new single-family house.

  • Plumbers working in town must be licensed by the Town.
  • The town keeps records of permitted projects, and copies are available through a Freedom of Information request.
  • Variance questions go to the Planning and Zoning Department.

If your file has gaps, ask for the records before you accept an offer. A buyer can then compare your paperwork to the house as it stands.

How does the Erie County Clerk record a Clarence deed?

The Erie County Clerk records deeds for Clarence parcels. The deed must be an original, signed and notarized, with a legal description and street addresses for all parties, since P.O. boxes are not accepted. A TP-584 tax affidavit goes in duplicate, and an RP-5217 transfer report is prepared on the state's site because its barcode cannot be reused from another transaction.

Fees are a $45 statutory recording fee, $5 per page, $10 to file the TP-584, and $125 for the RP-5217 on residential or farm property ($250 for other property). The seller pays New York State and Erie County transfer tax at filing. The combined rate is $4.50 per $500 of consideration, made up of $2.00 for the State and $2.50 for the County.

Owners aged 62 or older who have owned and lived in a one or two-family home for at least a year can claim a reduction to $2.00 per $500 by affidavit. A one percent mansion tax applies to residences of $1 million or more. Residential transfers also need a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form delivered to the Clerk at the time of transfer, and the finished original deed is mailed back to you after indexing.

More questions about Clarence, NY

How many people live in Clarence, NY?

The 2020 census counted 32,950 residents, a 7.4 percent increase over the 2010 count of 30,673. Clarence has no incorporated villages.

When is Grievance Day in Clarence?

It is the fourth Tuesday in May, which falls on May 25 in 2027. Use form RP-524 for the Board of Assessment Review, and use the informal review process earlier in the year if you only want the Assessor to look again.

Where do I pay Clarence property taxes?

Pay the Town Clerk at One Town Place, Clarence, NY 14031, by check, cash, mail or online. After June 30 unpaid town and county taxes move to Erie County Finance.

Do unpermitted repairs affect selling a Clarence house?

They can. The town says work without a required permit may hold up a sale and complicate an insurance claim, and a stop work order is possible. Ask the Building Department what a project needs to be closed out.

How much is transfer tax in Erie County?

The combined State and Erie County rate is $4.50 per $500 of price, paid by the seller at filing. Eligible senior owners aged 62 or older can reduce it to $2.00 per $500.

  • Harrison is in Westchester County.

How can a Harrison owner sell quickly?

Harrison owners can list through an agent, sell privately, or accept an as-is cash purchase, and only the last avoids staging, showings and renovation deadlines. With the Census median home value above $1 million, a rushed sale can cost a great deal, so weigh any offer against what similar Harrison houses have sold for.

Harrison is a combined town and village in Westchester County, about 27 miles from Grand Central. That setup creates local wrinkles for sellers: one building department for the whole municipality, a Receiver of Taxes who collects five times a year, and a county clerk who records the deed.

  • Agent listing: works for a house that is ready for the market and an owner with time to spare.
  • Private sale: saves commission but puts negotiation and paperwork on you.
  • Cash purchase: for estates, unfinished projects, tenant-occupied homes or a fixed deadline.

How expensive is housing in Harrison, by the Census?

QuickFacts shows 32,273 people in Harrison as of July 2025, against 28,218 counted in 2020. Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $1,010,700 for 2020 to 2024, and 60.5% of homes are owned by their occupants.

Rents are high too, at a median $2,616 a month. Median household income reaches $164,250 in 2024 dollars across 9,222 households averaging 2.88 people, and 60.4% of adults have at least a bachelor's degree. The mean trip to work is 29.2 minutes. Because the median value sits just over $1 million, a large share of Harrison sales reach the level where New York's 1% mansion tax, paid by the buyer, applies.

Land area is 16.77 square miles, which gives about 1,683 residents per square mile at the 2020 count.

How is Harrison arranged, and what does each area offer a buyer?

Harrison is shaped roughly like a figure eight, with downtown Harrison in the south and the hamlets of Purchase and West Harrison to the north. Founded under a patent in 1696 and made a town in 1788, it became a combined town and village in 1975.

Downtown divides into four sections: Brentwood Plaza, Sunny Ridge, Sterling Ridge/The Trails and the Village part of Harrison, with Halstead Avenue as its main street. West Harrison, around Lake Street and Silver Lake Park, has few road entrances. Purchase holds Manhattanville University, SUNY Purchase and, through its corporate campuses along I-287, the area known as the Platinum Mile. Harrison station on Metro-North's New Haven Line is the commuter link, and Westchester County Airport lies almost entirely within Purchase.

Much of the older housing dates from the 1920s through the 1950s. The Sunny Ridge subdivision was laid out on a former farm after 1929, and most of its houses went up from the mid-1940s on, in colonial revival and Tudor styles. Sites on the National Register include the Hadden-Margolis House, built around 1750, and the 1938 Post Office. Owners of period homes should keep records of past renovations, since buyers of older houses ask for them.

  • Roads: I-95, I-287, I-684 and the Hutchinson River Parkway, plus NY 120, 120A and 127.
  • Bus: the Bee-Line system.
  • Employers: corporate headquarters including MasterCard and PepsiCo.

Which schools serve Harrison homes?

The Harrison Central School District runs Harrison High School and Louis M. Klein Middle School, both downtown, plus four elementary schools. Purchase School covers Purchase and the north of West Harrison, Preston covers the Silver Lake area, Parsons covers south downtown, and Harrison Avenue School covers the rest of downtown.

Elementary attendance zones follow neighborhoods, so an address in Sunny Ridge and one in Purchase feed different schools. Higher education is nearby as well: Manhattanville University and SUNY Purchase are in Purchase, and Fordham opened a Westchester campus in West Harrison in 2008. Keio Academy of New York, a private high school, is also in Purchase.

How does Harrison assess and collect property tax?

The Assessor's Office maintains a record card for each of roughly 7,000 parcels and values them on current sales and cost, then applies the tax rate to produce each bill. The Receiver of Taxes collects town, village, school, county and state tax from a single office in the Municipal Building.

Harrison assessment and tax calendar (source: Town/Village of Harrison Assessor and Receiver of Taxes)
DateEvent
May 1Taxable status date; exemptions due
June 1Tentative roll filed; grievance period opens
Third Tuesday in JuneGrievance period ends
September 15Final roll filed
February and JuneTown and village tax due
January and SeptemberSchool tax due
AprilCounty and state tax due

Bills are mailed before the first of the month and must be paid by the month's last day, though mailing them is a courtesy and a lost bill does not excuse a late payment. The town says roughly 56% of collections go to schools, 25% to the town and 19% to the county. Changes of ownership should be reported to the tax office in writing.

What permits does Harrison require, and why do they matter at sale?

Harrison requires a building permit for new buildings, additions, alterations and accessory structures, and the Building Inspector issues the Certificate of Occupancy. A buyer's attorney will look for both on any house with visible improvements.

Most residential construction needs Architectural Board of Review approval, and permits cover sheds, decks, pools, interior alterations, fences, driveways, tree removal, plumbing and electrical work. The department may ask for a final as-built survey after new construction, additions, accessory structures, fences, walls or altered driveways. The Assessor learns of completed work from the permit and inspects with the Building Inspector, then adjusts the assessment, so unpermitted additions can surface as both a code problem and a higher bill.

  • Collect permits and Certificates of Occupancy for each improvement.
  • Find the most recent survey; the department wants 36 by 48 inches at standard size.
  • Counter hours run 9am to 5pm, and applications go in person or by mail rather than electronically.

What does recording a deed in Westchester cost?

The Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division records Harrison deeds. Its fee schedule lists a $45 statutory fee, $5 per written page, $5 for the TP-584 form on residential property and $125 for the RP-5217 transfer report, so a three-page residential deed in one municipality costs $190.

New York's transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up, and the clerk's own example turns a $404,501 sale into $1,620. At Harrison's $1,010,700 median value the same calculation gives $4,044. The seller normally pays it; the 1% mansion tax at $1 million or more falls on the buyer. The clerk steers filers to its PREP portal to work out the fees due.

More questions about Harrison, NY

Does Harrison have separate town and village taxes?

Harrison is one combined town and village, and the Receiver of Taxes collects both, with payments due in February and June. School tax is billed separately for January and September, and county and state tax in April.

When can a Harrison owner contest an assessment?

The grievance period runs from June 1, when the tentative roll is filed, to the third Tuesday in June. The Assessor sets May 1 as the date exemptions are due, and the final roll is filed September 15.

Is a permit needed for a deck or shed in Harrison?

Yes. Sheds, decks, pools and interior alterations all need permits, and most residential construction also needs Architectural Board of Review approval. The Building Inspector issues the Certificate of Occupancy.

What does the buyer pay on a million-dollar Harrison sale?

A 1% mansion tax applies when a residence sells for $1 million or more, and the buyer pays it. The seller covers New York's base transfer tax of $2 per $500, paid at recording.

Where is a Harrison deed filed?

With the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. A recording needs the deed, form TP-584, form RP-5217 and the filing fees, which the clerk's PREP portal can calculate.

Is Newburgh a town or a city, and why does it matter when selling?

There are two Newburghs in Orange County, and the Census figures used on this page describe the town. The city of Newburgh, a separate municipality on the river, was part of the town until it was rechartered in 1865. Since then it has been fully independent, independent of the town.

In 2020 the town had 31,985 residents and the city and town together had 60,842. The town passed the city in population for the first time in the 2010 census. If your deed or tax bill says Newburgh, confirm which municipality issued it before you look up dates and rules.

The rest of this page covers the town: its land, its tax calendar, its school districts and the offices a seller deals with.

What is the land like in the town of Newburgh?

The town covers 43.36 square miles of land, hilly in the middle and bounded on the east by the Hudson River. Steep bluffs line most of the shoreline, so very few houses have easy river access. The northern line and about a third of the western line touch Ulster County.

Several hills top 750 feet. Cronomer Hill, at 725 feet, is the central landmark, and most of it is a county-owned park with an observation tower that looks toward the Newburgh-Beacon Bridge and Stewart Airport. On hilly lots like these, a survey and a look at drainage are worth doing before you list.

Named areas include Balmville, Gardnertown, Orange Lake, Fostertown and Algonquin Park, home to the town's only historic district built around old gunpowder mills. Newburgh is also one of eight towns in Orange County with no incorporated villages inside it.

What is the history behind the Newburgh town name and its farmland?

German Palatine refugees settled the area in 1709 under the name Neuburg, and Scottish immigrants soon joined them. The area became a precinct in 1762 and a town in 1788. When Rockland County was cut from Orange in 1798, Newburgh and other southern Ulster towns were moved into Orange County.

The town stayed rural into the twentieth century, with apple orchards in the north and dairy and vegetable farms elsewhere. The postwar years turned farmland into subdivisions and school sites. Some of that history is still visible today: the PepsiCo bottling plant stands where a Little League ballpark once did, and Wedgewood Park, planned in the 1960s, was not finished until the late 1980s.

Expect a spread of ages in the housing stock, from farmhouses to 1980s developments.

What do the roads and the airport do for house values in Newburgh?

The town calls itself the "Crossroads of the Northeast," and the map backs it up: Interstate 84 runs east to west, the New York State Thruway (I-87) runs north to south, and a direct ramp between the two opened in December 2009. Route 300 is the main commercial strip, with Routes 9W, 17K, 32, 52 and 207 also crossing the town.

Stewart International Airport sits partly in the town, though mostly in New Windsor, and much of the land around it became Stewart State Forest. Most roads are maintained by the town highway department, two are county roads, and the town also has many private roads. If your house is on a private road, ask who plows and repairs it before you list.

The Census Bureau lists 2022 retail sales per capita at $37,920 in the town, above New Rochelle ($19,931) and New Windsor ($11,352) and close to New York City ($20,303).

What do Census numbers show about Newburgh homes and buyers?

Newburgh is a town of owners, with 79.8 percent of homes owner-occupied. The Census Bureau puts the median home value at $375,700 and median gross rent at $2,159 for 2020 to 2024, which is higher rent than in New Windsor next door.

  • Households: 11,640, with 2.71 people each
  • Median household income: $111,615 in 2024 dollars
  • Poverty rate: 7.3 percent
  • Estimated population change since 2020: down 0.5 percent
  • Mean commute: 36.6 minutes

The 2022 business figures show $1,207,597,000 in retail sales, $196,134,000 in transportation and warehousing receipts and $148,831,000 in health care and social assistance revenue for the town.

Most residents have lived in the same house for years. The Census shows 93.1 percent in the same home one year earlier, so few households move in any given year.

Who bills me for taxes in Newburgh, and what are the key dates?

The Receiver of Taxes bills property tax, but school tax depends on your district, because four of them serve the town: Marlboro, Wallkill, Valley Central and the Newburgh Enlarged City School District. Who collects the school bill depends on the district:

  • Marlboro: the town Receiver collects it
  • Valley Central: the town Receiver collects it
  • Wallkill: the district's own tax collector
  • Newburgh Enlarged City School District: the district's own tax collector
DateTown of Newburgh assessment or billing step
March 1Taxable status date and exemption filing deadline
May 1Tentative roll and assessment change notices
Fourth Tuesday in MayGrievance Day
July 1Final assessment roll filed
SeptemberMarlboro and Valley Central school tax due without penalty
OctoberSame school taxes carry a 2 percent penalty
JanuaryFull property tax bill due without penalty

Source: Town of Newburgh Assessor and Receiver of Taxes pages. The town has 13,027 taxable parcels.

The Receiver does not allow partial payments or installments on property tax. Water and sewer bills come four times a year, with a 5 percent penalty after 30 days, and unpaid amounts are added to the next year's property tax bill. That last rule is worth knowing: a water balance can land on the property's next tax bill unless it is settled at closing.

What offices handle exemptions, permits and the deed?

The Assessor handles exemptions, including STAR, veterans, senior citizen, disability and agricultural ones. Ask the office which of them are on your parcel. Its page links the state's Basic and Enhanced STAR credit registration and forms for the alternative veterans, Cold War veterans, low-income disability and senior citizen exemptions. The Code Compliance Department issues building permits and certificates of occupancy for new and existing structures and investigates code complaints.

The deed itself is recorded with the Orange County Clerk, and the state transfer tax return, Form TP-584, goes to the same office within 15 days after the deed is delivered. The state tax is $2 for each $500 of price, and by default the seller pays it. The Clerk says a copy of your deed costs about $5 directly from the office, so avoid third-party companies that charge more.

When a cash buyer takes the house as-is, the same paperwork still applies. Closing the file with the clerk and settling water, sewer and tax balances is what finishes the sale.

More questions about Newburgh, NY

Is the Census population on this page for the town or the city of Newburgh?

It is for the town, which the Census Bureau estimates at 31,825 residents in 2025. The city of Newburgh is a separate municipality and is not included in that figure.

When is Grievance Day in the town of Newburgh?

The fourth Tuesday in May. The tentative roll comes out May 1, and the final roll is filed July 1.

Who collects school tax in the town of Newburgh?

It depends on the district. The town's Receiver collects for Marlboro and Valley Central, while Wallkill and the Newburgh Enlarged City School District use their own collectors.

Can I pay Newburgh property tax in installments?

No. The Receiver says installments and partial payments are not allowed for property tax, so the January amount is the full bill, and penalties start if you pay in February or March.

Do unpaid water bills affect a Newburgh house sale?

Yes. Unpaid water and sewer bills are added to the next year's property tax bill, so settle them at or before closing.

Where is Cicero, NY, and what is the town like?

Cicero is a lakeside suburb of Syracuse in the northeastern part of Onondaga County. Oneida Lake lies along its northern edge, the Oneida River marks the border with Oswego County, and Chittenango Creek marks the line with Madison County. The town covers about 48.5 square miles, and a large swamp, Cicero Swamp, sits in its southeastern part.

The town began in 1790 as a township in the Central New York Military Tract, separated from Lysander in 1807, and lost its western half in 1827 when that portion became the town of Clay. Interstate 81, U.S. Route 11 and Routes 31 and 298 pass through, and the reconstructed Erie Canal follows the Oneida River along the north line. A small corner of Syracuse Hancock International Airport reaches the southern town line, and Michael Airfield, a single-runway general aviation field, is inside the town.

Which neighborhoods and school districts shape a Cicero sale?

Much of the town is wetland, forest and farm land, with a growing number of housing developments pushing onto the farmland. Hamlets include Brewerton near the northern line, Bridgeport (partly in Madison County), Cicero Center on Route 31, and shoreline settlements such as Kraus Landing, Forest Beach and Lower South Bay. The Village of North Syracuse lies partly inside the town on its western edge.

Four school districts bill taxes on Cicero parcels. The town's tax receiver processes school taxes for North Syracuse Central Schools, and for the Chittenango, Central Square and East Syracuse-Minoa districts on properties in the town. Buyers will ask which district serves an address, so confirm it from the school line on the tax bill.

  • Subdivisions named in local descriptions include Bay Colony near South Bay, The Crossings, and Lyon's Runne near Oneida Lake.
  • Lakeshore settlements such as Kraus Landing and Valentine's Beach sit on Oneida Lake north of Cicero Center.
  • Interstate 81 and U.S. 11 meet near the hamlet of Cicero in the southwest.

How is a Cicero house assessed, and when is the next Grievance Day?

The Assessor's office values every parcel in Cicero, handles veteran, senior and disability exemptions, and tracks sales data and the equalization rate. The tentative roll was published May 1, 2026, and the town reports a 53 percent level of assessment, an equalization rate of 53 percent and a residential assessment ratio of 53 percent. A house assessed at $150,000 would therefore be viewed as having a market value of roughly $283,000 under that ratio.

The 2026 Grievance Day has already passed. The town posts the next Board of Assessment Review date as Tuesday, May 25, 2027, with hearings by appointment only at the Cicero Town Meeting Room, 8236 Brewerton Road, from 12 to 2 p.m. and 6 to 8 p.m. Complaints must be filed by 3:00 p.m. that day on form RP-524, and the town accepts them in the Town Hall drop box, by mail or by email.

  • Taxable status date is March 1, and the town page says completed exemption applications may be submitted through March 1, 2027.
  • From 2026 the State decides who qualifies for the Basic and Enhanced STAR exemptions, so questions about STAR go to the State, not the Assessor.
  • Informal reviews with the Assessor happen before Grievance Day, and the final roll is dated July 1.

When are Cicero property tax bills due?

Cicero's Receiver of Taxes processes the town and county bill, the North Syracuse village bill and the school bills. The town and county bill is mailed around January 1 and is due without penalty on February 2. School bills are mailed around September 1 and are due without penalty around October 1. Village bills (for the part of North Syracuse in town) are mailed around June 1 and due July 1.

Partial payments are accepted if nothing delinquent is owed, and the first payment must reach the office by the no-penalty date. Town and county bills can be split into up to four payments, village bills into three, and school bills into three. Mail counts as paid on its postmark date, but a postage meter mark does not count.

The tax office has one caution for sellers. It takes two to three months after a deed is filed with the county for the Assessor's records to reflect the new owner, so call the tax office when you buy or sell. Until the records change, the bill goes to the owner on file.

What do Cicero zoning and code rules mean for a seller?

The Department of Zoning and Planning issues building permits and enforces the town code from the Town Hall on Brewerton Road. A Certificate of Occupancy is issued once all work under a permit is complete and outside inspection certificates for plumbing and electrical have been received. Anything built without a permit cannot receive a Certificate of Occupancy or a Certificate of Compliance, and the town may issue a stop work order and fines.

Residents are told to find their zoning on the tax bill or the town zoning map. The office lists these permit triggers.

  • Permits are needed to add on, demolish, change occupancy, move doors and windows, repair fire damage or install a fence.
  • Fireplaces, woodstoves and heat-producing devices also need permits.
  • Ordinary repairs, siding, roofing over no more than two layers, and windows or doors of equal size need no permit.
  • A permit lasts 12 months from issue.

Plan review for a new dwelling can run two to six weeks, so an unpermitted addition is better settled before you list.

How is a deed recorded for a Cicero house in Onondaga County?

Deeds for Cicero parcels are recorded by the Onondaga County Clerk, and county records reach back to 1794. The base fee for a deed is $45.50 plus $5 per page, and transfer tax is $4 per thousand dollars of price. A TP-584 return costs $5, the RP-5217 form costs $125 for improved residential or agricultural property and $250 for improved commercial property or vacant land, and a $10 charge applies to residential deeds.

State law puts the base transfer tax on the seller, at $2 for every $500 of price, and the TP-584 is due within 15 days of the deed. Recording is also where a mansion tax of 1 percent attaches to residences at $1 million or more, and the buyer pays it. The clerk's office closes every first Tuesday of the month from 10:30 to 11:00 a.m. for a staff meeting, which is a small thing worth knowing if you are timing a closing run.

More questions about Cicero, NY

How many people live in Cicero, New York?

The 2020 census counted 31,435 residents, down 0.8 percent from the 31,682 counted in 2010.

When is Grievance Day for Cicero property owners?

The Cicero assessor posts Tuesday, May 25, 2027 as the next Board of Assessment Review date. Complaints must be in by 3:00 p.m. that day, and hearings are by appointment.

Who do I pay Cicero property taxes to?

Pay the Cicero Receiver of Taxes at Town Hall, 8236 Brewerton Road, Cicero, NY 13039. The office collects town, county, village and school taxes for parcels in town.

Can I sell a Cicero house that has unpermitted work?

You can sell it, but the town cannot issue a Certificate of Occupancy or Compliance for work done without a permit. Call Zoning and Planning to learn what the town would require.

What does the county charge to record a deed in Onondaga County?

The base fee is $45.50 plus $5 per page, with $5 for the TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217 on residential property. Transfer tax is $4 per thousand dollars of price.
